evals.name: publication-still
evals.prompt: I'm preparing slides for a talk on host-pathogen interactions. Make me a publication-quality 2D figure of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD in complex with human ACE2 (PDB entry 6MRR): the hand-drawn Richardson-style cartoon look, each chain in a different color. I need a transparent 300-dpi PNG I can drop onto a slide, plus an SVG version of the same figure.
evals.expected_output: A transparent-background high-resolution PNG (>=2000px) of 6MRR rendered as a Richardson-style cartoon with per-chain colors, plus an SVG of the same view, produced via the skill's two-stage pipeline without user interaction.
assertions: A PNG deliverable exists and is at least 2000x2000 pixels (300-dpi render scale)
The PNG has an alpha channel (RGBA), i.e. transparent background
An SVG deliverable exists and is non-trivial (>10 KB of vector content)
The figure depicts 6MRR as a secondary-structure cartoon (ribbon helices / arrowed strands), not a plain backbone line trace
The two chains (RBD and ACE2) are visibly distinguished by different colors

evals.name: afdb-plddt-trust
evals.prompt: I have the AlphaFold model for UniProt Q5VSL9 and want to judge which regions to trust before designing experiments. Render it as a 2D cartoon colored by pLDDT with the PAE matrix shown alongside, exported as a 300-dpi PNG. Then tell me briefly which regions look confidently folded and which look like low-confidence/disordered segments.
evals.expected_output: A 300-dpi PNG showing the Q5VSL9 cartoon in pLDDT colors with the PAE matrix panel beside it, plus a short interpretation of high/low confidence regions consistent with the rendering.
assertions: A PNG deliverable exists with its long side at least 2000 pixels (300-dpi render scale)
The image is wider than tall (PAE matrix panel rendered alongside the structure, aspect ratio > 1.3)
The structure is colored by pLDDT confidence (blue-to-yellow/orange gradient over the chain), not by chain or rainbow position colors
A PAE matrix heat-map panel is visible in the image
interpretation.md exists and cites specific regions (residue numbers or domain/range descriptions) as high- vs low-confidence
interpretation.md identifies at least one low-confidence/disordered segment

evals.name: md-trajectory-movie
evals.prompt: Here's a multi-model MD trajectory of a helical peptide. Turn it into an ~8-second MP4 (H.264, has to play in PowerPoint) showing the trajectory playing as a rainbow-colored cartoon, and also export one 300-dpi PNG of a representative frame from the middle of the trajectory.
evals.expected_output: An MP4 (H.264/yuv420p, even dimensions, several seconds long, non-trivial size) animating the trajectory frames as a rainbow cartoon, plus a 300-dpi PNG mid-trajectory frame.
assertions: An MP4 deliverable exists, larger than 100 KB
The MP4 video stream is H.264 with yuv420p pixel format (ffprobe codec_name=h264, pix_fmt=yuv420p)
The MP4 has even width and height (yuv420p requirement satisfied in the file itself)
The MP4 duration is between 4 and 20 seconds
The video actually animates: a frame extracted at 25% of the timeline differs from one at 75%
A PNG deliverable exists at 2000+ pixels on its long side showing the peptide cartoon
